name: Bunt / Tuluva (Mulki) wedding traditions
tagline: Dhare, tulsi puja and maternal‑uncle roles — Tuluva weddings of northern Kasaragod
summary: The Tuluva (Bunt/Mulki) weddings in northern Kasaragod follow a coastal Tulu‑Nadu ritual script — dhare, tulsi katta, murtha and strong maternal‑clan roles — distinct from central Kerala practice.…
description: Tuluva (Bunt / Mulki) weddings in northern Kasaragod follow the Tulu‑Nadu ritual order: a ritual bath, tulsi prayers, murtha rites and the dhare ceremony where holy water is poured over the couple’s joined hands. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))

These weddings matter because they preserve matrilineal and bari (mother’s clan) customs, distinctive jewellery and procession patterns that differ from central Kerala’s Vedic‑style kanyadaan and homa centred weddings. ([velvetknot.in](https://velvetknot.in/tulu-bunt-wedding-traditions/))

A visitor who sees a Tuluva wedding gets vivid coastal rituals: jasmine‑studded plaits, gold patti and vanki ornaments, ritual rice showers, and regional performing arts that sometimes appear alongside family rites. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))
highlights: Dhare: pouring holy water over joined hands — ceremonial heart of the day. ([tacproductions.in](https://tacproductions.in/blog/tulu-wedding-rituals/))
Tulsi katta (tulsi plant prayer) and separate ritual bath (mangala snana) at each home. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))
Strong role for the bride’s maternal kin and historic bari (matrilineal) rules. ([velvetknot.in](https://velvetknot.in/tulu-bunt-wedding-traditions/))
Distinctive bride ornaments: patti (waistbelt), vanki (armlet), mundale (maang tikka) and jasmine plait. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))
Local ritual arts (Mangalamkali / regional Theyyam/Bhuta echoes) may appear at celebrations. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavilan?utm_source=openai))

sections.heading: Background
body: Tuluva Bunts across Dakshina Kannada, Udupi and northern Kasaragod share a wedding culture that developed independently from central Kerala and mainstream Kannada rites; the region is traditionally called Tulunadu and keeps its own calendar and clan rules. ([velvetknot.in](https://velvetknot.in/tulu-bunt-wedding-traditions/))

Historically some Tuluva groups followed matrilineal (aliyasantana) patterns; while modern practice varies, the bride’s maternal relatives retain ceremonial responsibilities in many families. ([velvetknot.in](https://velvetknot.in/tulu-bunt-wedding-traditions/))

sections.heading: Key rituals and sequence
body: Pre‑wedding: female elders perform the ritual bath (mangala snana) at each home; the bride wears a new silk sari and is decorated with jasmine flowers and traditional gold pieces. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))

Dhare (the central rite): elders hold a chembu (spouted vessel) and pour sacred water over the couple’s joined hands while the groom ties the mangala sutra; the bride’s maternal uncle plays a defined role during this moment. Photographers note dhare is a single, decisive moment. ([tacproductions.in](https://tacproductions.in/blog/tulu-wedding-rituals/))

Post‑dare rites: rice showers, seven steps around a symbolic fire in some families, a formal welcome of the bride into the groom’s family and a large coastal feast with regional dishes. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))

sections.heading: Local flavour and performing arts
body: Tuluva weddings in Kasaragod often sit alongside local devotional and folk practices — Bhuta/Theyam traces, Mangalamkali and community songs — reflecting the district’s multi‑lingual, multi‑ritual identity. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavilan?utm_source=openai))

Some northern Kasaragod communities retain uncommon rites (for example, community‑reported 'ghost marriages' in the district for specific social reasons) — these are sensitive, community‑specific practices and should be understood as living tradition rather than universal. ([timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/marriage-of-ghosts-still-prevalent-among-kasaragod-communities/articleshow/61514600.cms))

sections.heading: What a visitor should expect
body: Weddings are group‑centred, musical and fast‑moving at key moments; you will see a mix of Malayalam, Tulu and Kannada in use and ceremonial items not common in central Kerala weddings. ([pdfcoffee.com](https://pdfcoffee.com/tulu-studies-pdf-free.html?utm_source=openai))

If you are invited, observe reverence during dhare and murtha, accept photography limits (dare is a one‑take moment) and ask permission before touching ritual objects. ([tacproductions.in](https://tacproductions.in/blog/tulu-wedding-rituals/))

latest.text: Long updated feature summarising Tulu/Bunt wedding rites—dhare, bari and aliya‑santana—published and updated for 2026. Useful recent synthesis for observers. ([velvetknot.in](https://velvetknot.in/tulu-bunt-wedding-traditions/))

visitorInfo.bestTime: Year‑round; families fix dates by muhurtha (astrological timing) rather than a single wedding season. ([velvetknot.in](https://velvetknot.in/tulu-bunt-wedding-traditions/))
visitorInfo.howToReach: Northern Kasaragod is served by Kasaragod and Kanhangad railway stations on the Mangalore–Palakkad line; the nearest major airport is Mangaluru International Airport. Local Tulu‑speaking villages are reached by road from Kasaragod town. Confirm exact village directions with hosts. ([irisholidays.com](https://www.irisholidays.com/bekal?utm_source=openai))
etiquette: Dhare is a single sacred moment — ask hosts before photographing or stepping forward. ([tacproductions.in](https://tacproductions.in/blog/tulu-wedding-rituals/))
Respect the maternal‑uncle and sumangali (senior married women) roles — they may lead key rituals and blessings. ([bunts.org.uk](https://bunts.org.uk/about/bunts-culture/))

Dress modestly and match the formality: traditional silk sarees and understated jewellery are appropriate for invited guests; confirm dress expectations with the family. ([mangaloreheritage.com](https://mangaloreheritage.com/bunt-traditions/bunt-wedding-traditions/))

Language note: Tulu, Kannada and Malayalam commonly mix — a polite inquiry in Malayalam or English is usually welcome if you don’t know Tulu. ([pdfcoffee.com](https://pdfcoffee.com/tulu-studies-pdf-free.html?utm_source=openai))
